linkedin.about: Steven Bartlett is a 33-year-old British entrepreneur, investor in more than 100 companies, speaker, author, and media owner. He is the founder of Steven.com - the creator media company. Through it's podcast creator "label" called FlightStory, they create and scales new media podcast IP and commercialise that IP through brand partnerships, programmatic revenue, events, book publishing, newsletters, e-commerce, and new product development. He is also the co-founder of thirdweb, a developer platform powering over 100,000 teams to build and launch web3 applications, and FlightCast, a video-first podcast hosting platform used by some of the world’s largest shows. Steven first gained recognition as the co-founder and CEO of Social Chain AG, a social media marketing and e-commerce company he launched at 21 and took public on a European stock exchange by the age of 27 via reverse merger. Social Chain AG became a globally recognised business with hundreds of employees across London, Manchester, Berlin, New York, and Los Angeles, working with major brands including Amazon, Apple, and Coca-Cola. Through his Fund and personal investments, he has backed companies including SpaceX, Huel, ZOE, Whoop, MrBeast, Groq, KetoneIQ, Cadence, PerfectTed, and over 60 others - focusing on businesses that improve human health, happiness, and performance. Steven is also the creator and host of The Diary of a CEO, currently the world's most downloaded / watched podcast and the fastest-growing podcast in the world. He is the youngest-ever investor on BBC’s Dragons’ Den. linkedin.activityText: Steven Bartlett Steven Bartlett 2h Steven Bartlett shared this He infiltrated criminal networks in Colombia because normal life was boring. This is Shawn Ryan. He joined the US Navy at 17, became a Navy SEAL, went on to work as a CIA contractor, and has since built one of the biggest podcasts in the world. When we sat down, I told Shawn that it feels like he has lived several different lives. And I don’t think I’ve ever meant that more literally. One of the most unexpected parts of his story is what happened to his faith. He told me about an experience where he believes he saw hell, describing it as complete emptiness, fear and the absence of God. For someone who has spent so much of his life around war, danger and intelligence, it was this experience that seemed to have changed him in a completely different way. And that is only one chapter of his life. We discussed things like: -⁠ ⁠Why he went to Colombia and embedded himself inside criminal networks. -⁠ ⁠Why he says he went to hell and came back seeing faith differently. - ⁠What he saw across Haiti, Afghanistan and Iraq that he still remembers today. - ⁠How podcasts could be used to manipulate millions of people. - ⁠Why politicians lying to his face changed how he sees politics. - ⁠Why he thinks China benefits every time America weakens itself. What makes Shawn’s perspective so interesting is that he hasn’t just studied these worlds from the outside. He has lived inside many of them. There were things in this conversation I probably would have dismissed several years ago. But doing this podcast has made me far more careful about assuming I understand what is possible. You don’t have to agree with everything Shawn believes. But his perspective is absolutely worth hearing. Out now on all platforms ❤️👊🏾 The Diary Of A CEO Steven Bartlett Steven Bartlett 3d Steven Bartlett shared this 13,000 employees became 3 in the space of one week. It’s quite difficult to comprehend what that would do to a person. Adam Neumann is the co-founder of WeWork. He grew the company to a $47 billion valuation before its failed IPO, his departure as CEO and one of the most public corporate collapses in recent history. I’ve met hundreds of extraordinary people doing this podcast, but within a few minutes of meeting Adam I realised he was quite unlike almost any founder or CEO I’ve met before. There’s a depth, philosophy and perspective to him that is incredibly rare. So I wanted to understand where that came from and what the last few years had actually done to him. We talked about: - His relationship with money and where it went wrong. - The friends who disappeared when everything changed. - The mistakes he made as a leader. - Why he now surrounds himself with people willing to tell him no. - Why he disconnects from technology for 24 hours every week. SOME NEWS 🚨 this year I’m joining @sharktankabc !!! 📺 🇺🇸 this was a dream of mine AND my mums...let me explain👇🏾

My nigerian mum raised 4 of us without being able to read or write herself, having left school when she was a child in Nigeria.

I struggled with school too - I wasn’t a smart kid and couldn’t pay attention, so I quickly realised the “traditional path” wasn’t going to work for someone like me

Then, when I was 12 years old, I discovered Dragons’ Den! 🐉

Me and my mum both fell in love with the show. Looking back, I think entrepreneurship offered us both hope - a path to a better life for people like us, who couldn’t pass tests in a classroom but were willing to work hard.

At 12 I would pause the TV and give my verdict, as if I was the 6th Dragon

By 16 I’d discovered Shark Tank and was starting my first (terrible) businesses

By 18 I was a university dropout with a start-up

And somehow, 9 years later, I ended up sitting in one of those Dragons’ Den chairs I used to shout at from our sofa

My mum has never fully gotten over it. 

When I call her today, 6 years later, the conversation is still 80% Dragons’ Den - her opinion on what I said, the businesses, what SHE would have done...

Btw, i’m genuinely not sure if she knows I have a podcast 😂 i don’t think she’s ever mentioned it 😅

But she knows Dragons’ Den, and that’s more than enough for her.

I know she’s always wanted me to do Shark Tank, so this phone call - telling her that day had come absolutely made my day, and hopefully her’s too!

I very much hope to do her proud + all of you that have supported me for the longest time... wish me luck!! 👊🏾❤️

P.S who would win in a fight, a shark 🦈 or a dragon 🐉 ???

analysis.name: Steven Bartlett
analysis.oneLiner: A visionary entrepreneur and media mogul, Steven built an empire from scratch, driven by curiosity, a desire for impact, and an insatiable hunger for growth.
analysis.summary: Steven Bartlett is a highly driven and successful entrepreneur, investor, and media personality. He founded Social Chain at 21, took it public by 27, and is now the force behind Steven.com, FlightStory, and the massively popular podcast 'The Diary of a CEO'. His work focuses on the creator economy, health, happiness, and performance, reflecting a deep curiosity about human potential and societal impact. He's a strategic thinker who values continuous learning, meaningful connections, and challenging conventional wisdom, all while maintaining a grounded perspective on his humble beginnings.

needs.detail: Instagram post: 'True, deep relationships require your total, undivided presence.. not just the spare moments between notifications...'. This suggests he values genuine, focused interaction.

personality.note: Highly open, demonstrated by his podcast exploring diverse perspectives, interest in global affairs, and willingness to challenge his own assumptions ('doing this podcast has made me far more careful about assuming I understand what is possible').
Extremely high conscientiousness, evident in his rapid career progression, founding multiple successful companies, and consistent output of high-quality content. He is goal-oriented and disciplined.

High extraversion, as a public speaker, podcast host, and CEO of global companies. He thrives in social, interactive, and high-visibility roles, and actively engages with his audience on social media.

Moderately agreeable. While he values relationships and collaboration (co-founder roles), his entrepreneurial drive and willingness to challenge norms suggest he's not afraid to be assertive or hold strong opinions. He also shares advice that can be direct ('Stop Saying Yes').

High emotional stability. He discusses growing up in an 'unstable environment' and adapting, then building a massive career, indicating resilience and a calm, focused approach under pressure. His posts are generally reflective and composed.

lifestyle.label: Pace
lifestyle.value: Extremely fast-paced, high-achieving, and constantly evolving with multiple ventures and investments.

lifestyle.label: Social energy
lifestyle.value: Highly social, involving frequent public speaking, interviews, networking, and managing large teams across global offices.

lifestyle.label: Fitness
lifestyle.value: Implied focus on health and performance through investments (Huel, ZOE, Whoop, KetoneIQ) and general 'human performance' interest, but no direct evidence of personal fitness routine.

lifestyle.label: Travel
lifestyle.value: Extensive international travel, managing global companies (London, LA, NYC, Berlin), and photos show him on a private jet.

lifestyle.label: Work-life
lifestyle.value: Work-integrated, with his career being a central part of his identity and lifestyle, often blurring lines between work and personal interests (e.g., birthday on a private jet with laptops).

analysis.communicationStyle: Direct, articulate, insightful, and often motivational. He uses storytelling (Shawn Ryan interview) and personal anecdotes (his mum, his struggles in school) to connect, but also provides clear, actionable advice.
analysis.loveLanguage: Quality Time (focused, undivided presence) and Words of Affirmation (through intellectual exchange and appreciation of growth/effort).
analysis.lookingFor: Someone intellectually curious, ambitious, and emotionally intelligent, who can appreciate and thrive within his dynamic, high-achieving lifestyle while also valuing deep, authentic connection and presence.
greenFlags: Deeply reflective and self-aware, often sharing insights on personal growth and psychology.
Incredibly driven and successful, yet grounded by his humble beginnings and appreciative of support (e.g., his mum's dream for Shark Tank).
Committed to continuous learning and understanding diverse perspectives.
Values authentic, present relationships over superficial interactions.
Invests in ventures that aim to improve human health and happiness, indicating a desire for positive impact.
watchOuts: His extremely demanding schedule and constant travel might make consistent, traditional relationship time challenging.
His public profile and high visibility mean a partner would also be in the public eye to some extent.
His focus on growth and achievement might overshadow other aspects if a partner isn't equally driven or understanding.
dealbreakers: Lack of ambition or intellectual curiosity.
Disinterest in personal growth or self-reflection.
Someone who doesn't understand or respect his demanding career and public life.
Superficiality or an inability to engage in deep, present conversations.
analysis.idealFirstDate: A thought-provoking conversation over dinner at a chic, intimate restaurant, followed by a walk where they can discuss a recent podcast episode, a book, or a complex idea they've both been pondering. The focus would be on intellectual connection and genuine presence.

I'll use vocabulary that reflects intellectual curiosity and ambition, occasionally referencing his entrepreneurial journey or podcast themes. I'll be direct but engaging, always seeking to understand and connect on a deeper level, mirroring his value for 'undivided presence.' Humour will be intelligent and subtle, perhaps a self-aware nod to the intensity of his work.
